Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

rich — having a lot of money. Example: It is a rich area.
poor — having little money. Example: It is a poor neighbourhood.
money — coins and notes used to buy things. Example: The flats cost a lot of money.
expensive — costing a lot of money. Example: The watch was expensive.
cheap — not expensive. Example: The gift was cheap.
area — a part of a city or country. Example: This is an expensive area.
neighbourhood — the area around your home. Example: The neighbourhood is poor.
live — to have your home somewhere. Example: Many families live in small flats.
afford — to have enough money for something. Example: I can't afford a new car.
city — a large town. Example: The city is busy.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• It is an expensive area.
• Many people live here.
• We don't have much money.
• I can't afford it.
• The neighbourhood is poor.

Grammar focus: Countable and uncountable nouns.
Use much with uncountable nouns and many with countable nouns: much money, many shops. Use can't afford for things that cost too much.
